summary: I reviewed the supplied diff (7 files, +519/-208) and the complete post-change budget module as review data only; I ran nothing. The change replaces a crate-visible `install() -> Guard` with a private `Guard`/`install` plus a crate-visible synchronous `with_budget<T>(&QueryBudget, impl FnOnce() -> T) -> T`. `install` now `replace`s ACTIVE (saving the prior `Limits`) and `replace`s EXCEEDED (saving the prior sticky reason); `Guard::drop` restores both verbatim, so a nested frame is exactly transparent on return, on `?`-error and on unwind. This is the correct minimal fix for #6476: pre-fix, any nested engine call from a user callback reset ACTIVE to OFF and EXCEEDED to None, permanently disarming the outer budget (including cancellation) for the remainder of the outer query. Soundness: the `CancelPtr`/`unsafe impl Send+Sync` remain pre-existing, but the justification is now actually correct rather than merely asserted. Because `Guard` is private, non-`Send` (`PhantomData<Rc<()>>`), constructible only inside `with_budget`, and never escapes that frame, LIFO nesting is mechanically unforgeable (no `mem::forget`, no out-of-order drop, no cross-thread move). By induction every `cancel` pointer in ACTIVE and every `previous.cancel` held by a live Guard is owned by a `QueryBudget` borrowed by a still-live enclosing frame on the same thread; ACTIVE/EXCEEDED are `Cell`s of `Copy`, non-`Drop`, const-initialised TLS, so `Guard::drop` cannot fail or panic during thread teardown. I checked all fourteen production migrations (cache::eval; construct::{construct_prepared,describe_prepared,construct_or_describe}_with_budget; explain::explain_analyze_with_budget; explain_json::explain_plan_analyze_with_budget; lib::{query_prepared,ask_prepared,query_json_prepared,query_json_chunks,query_json_stream_prepared,count_prepared}_with_budget; update::{update_in_place_prepared_with_budget,update_in_place_core}) — bodies are mechanically preserved, `?` still yields the same error to the same caller, view guards still outlive the budget scope and the trace guard still drops before the budget guard, and `set_query_base` keeps its position relative to install. All four synchronous snapshot consumers (scan SELECT-JSON at ~2840 via `parallel_json_fanout`, bindings SELECT-JSON at ~3039, parallel hash join at ~9102, residual anti-join at ~10070) take the snapshot inside the owning frame's dynamic extent and join by construction (`par_chunks().map().collect()`, `par_iter().fold().reduce()`, `par_iter().map().collect::<Result<_>>()` where `?` fires only after the collect joins); the parallel materialise path at ~2645 takes no snapshot and is correctly not enumerated. SERVICE ordering is sound: all three savepoint owners capture and restore within one frame, and a nested `with_budget` that fully returns in between (e.g. a user local-SERVICE handler running a nested query) restores the parent verbatim first, so `restore_bytes` writes the parent's `extra_bytes`/sticky back into the parent's own frame. Nested budget semantics are shadow-not-inherit with exact parent resumption, which is documented on `QueryBudget` and is strictly better than the pre-fix behaviour. I found no introduced defect and no blocking finding; the residual risks are feature-matrix compilation of the new `#[cfg(test)]` module and the un-run authoritative gates, which is precisely what protected CI exists to answer.

nonblocking_findings.location: crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs and cache.rs — `exec::set_query_base(...)` now called inside the `with_budget` closure; `crate::view_scope(&active)` guard taken outside it (all 14 call sites)
nonblocking_findings.observation: `set_query_base` is a plain per-query TLS write with no save/restore. A nested engine call from a callback (exactly the scenario the new `public_extension_nested_query_preserves_outer_cancel` test drives) overwrites the outer query's base IRI and never restores it; the `view_scope` guard's nested restore semantics are not visible in this patch.
nonblocking_findings.consequence: After this patch the budget is the only per-query TLS that is frame-transparent. Relative-IRI resolution in the remainder of the outer query can silently use the nested query's base; a `view_scope` guard that clears rather than restores would have the same shape of bug the budget just fixed.
nonblocking_findings.suggested_resolution: Out of scope for this change. File a follow-up to audit `set_query_base`, `view_scope`, `trace::install`, `functions`, `query_now`, `local_services` and `spatial` for save-previous/restore-previous semantics, ideally reusing the same private-guard idiom.

nonblocking_findings.classification: future-misuse risk, not a defect in this change
nonblocking_findings.location: crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs, `pub(in crate::exec) fn snapshot() -> Limits` and `pub(crate) fn with_budget<T>(...) -> T`
nonblocking_findings.observation: `Limits` is `Copy` with no lifetime parameter and `with_budget` returns an arbitrary `T`, so nothing type-level prevents a future exec-internal caller from returning a snapshot (or a struct containing one) out of its owning frame, or stashing one in a `static`/detached task.
nonblocking_findings.consequence: Such a use would produce a dangling `CancelPtr` dereferenced by an atomic load — UB, and not caught by any current test. Today no consumer does this and the visibility narrowing plus the doc comment bound the blast radius to `crate::exec`.
nonblocking_findings.suggested_resolution: Optional follow-up: either give the snapshot an invariant lifetime (`Limits<'a>` with `PhantomData<&'a QueryBudget>`) or expose a `with_snapshot(|l| ...)` seam so the value cannot outlive the frame. The prior design review explicitly declined to require this in this patch; I agree it is not required here.

nonblocking_findings.location: crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs, `byte_savepoint` / `restore_bytes` (`cfg(any(feature = "service", feature = "service-local"))`) and the three owners `eval_service`, `try_local_service`, `bound_join_to_endpoint`
nonblocking_findings.observation: The new doc comment correctly states the rule ("Never apply a savepoint while a different budget frame is active") but nothing enforces it. All current owners capture and restore inside one frame, and the only user code that can run in between (a local SERVICE handler) can only nest via the scoped `with_budget`, which fully pops before `restore_bytes` runs — so the current code is correct.
nonblocking_findings.consequence: A future caller that let a savepoint straddle an *entered* frame would write the parent's `extra_bytes`/sticky into a child's ACTIVE, masking a child's `max-bytes` exhaustion and corrupting the child's accounting.
nonblocking_findings.suggested_resolution: Add a monotonically increasing frame counter to `Limits` (bumped in `install`), copy it into `ByteSavepoint`, and `debug_assert_eq!` it in `restore_bytes`. Cheap, test-only cost, and it converts a comment into a checked invariant.

nonblocking_findings.location: crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs, `QueryBudget` doc addition; exec.rs `install` (child gets `extra_bytes: 0`, `byte_width: BYTES_PER_ID`, no inherited deadline/cancel)
nonblocking_findings.observation: A nested budget fully shadows the parent: the outer deadline and cancellation are not observed for the duration of a nested unlimited query invoked from a callback, and the nested query's byte charges are never accumulated into the parent.
nonblocking_findings.consequence: Cancellation latency for an outer query is bounded only by the duration of the callback plus its nested queries. This is strictly better than pre-fix (where the outer budget was destroyed outright) and is now accurately documented, but it is not a bounded-cancel-latency guarantee.
nonblocking_findings.suggested_resolution: None required. If a latency SLA is ever claimed, a follow-up could intersect the parent's cancel flag and `min(deadline)` into child frames; that is a semantic change and belongs in its own issue.

nonblocking_findings.location: crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs, `CancelPtr` doc and the two `unsafe impl` SAFETY comments
nonblocking_findings.observation: "Only the innermost frame writes ACTIVE" is not literally true — `set_width`, `restore_width`, `add_bytes` and `restore_bytes` also mutate ACTIVE (always on behalf of the innermost frame, and none of them changes `cancel`). The `Send`/`Sync` impls remain usage-level rather than type-level invariants.
nonblocking_findings.consequence: A future reader could over-trust the stated invariant. No behavioural impact.
nonblocking_findings.suggested_resolution: Reword to "only `install`/`Guard::drop` write the `cancel` pointer; the other ACTIVE writers only mutate width/bytes of the innermost frame", and state explicitly that the `Send`/`Sync` impls are justified by the module's private construction plus the four audited scoped-join consumers.

nonblocking_findings.location: crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs migrated `remaining_timeout` test (two closing `})` at the same wrong indent), the blank first line inside the `cancel_flag_zero_vs_one_trips_both_poll_paths` closure, and the incidental reflows of `Limits::bytes`, `Limits::why`, `remaining_timeout`, `cap_alloc`
nonblocking_findings.observation: The four reflows are rustfmt `chain_width`-driven and are behaviour-neutral noise mixed into a behavioural patch; the migrated `remaining_timeout` test is clearly not rustfmt output.
nonblocking_findings.consequence: If the repo enforces `cargo fmt --check`, the file may fail the gate; the noise also slightly enlarges the reviewed surface for no functional reason.
nonblocking_findings.suggested_resolution: Run the repo's fmt configuration over the touched regions before the CI run.

nonblocking_findings.observation: The savepoint test is the only new test that does not assert the idle post-frame state (`assert_state(OFF, None)`) after the outer `with_budget` returns. The public test asserts `std::thread::current().id() == owner` inside the callback, which holds only because the one-row projection plan stays serial.
nonblocking_findings.consequence: Minor: a regression that left residue after the savepoint test's outer frame would go unnoticed; the thread-identity assert would become brittle if projection/BIND evaluation were ever parallelised.
nonblocking_findings.suggested_resolution: Add the trailing `assert_state(OFF, None)` for symmetry, and either drop the thread-identity assert or comment that it pins the serial single-row plan.

nonblocking_findings.classification: coverage scope statement (not a code defect)
nonblocking_findings.location: task-private observer delta (absent from committed source), scan SELECT-JSON fanout at exec.rs ~2847
nonblocking_findings.observation: Dynamic two-worker evidence exists for one of the four snapshot fanouts only, via a probe that is not in production. The other three rest on source audit.
nonblocking_findings.consequence: The audit is sound as written — `collect`, `fold`+`reduce` and `collect::<Result<_>>` all join before the value is observed, and all four sites are lexically inside the owning frame — but there is no dynamic witness that a snapshot cannot outlive its frame on those paths.
nonblocking_findings.suggested_resolution: None required for CI admission; if cheap, run the engine's existing parallel join/anti-join tests under a thread sanitiser or Miri (see CI obligations) rather than adding production instrumentation.

design_conditions_assessment.private_guard_and_install_in_same_patch: Met. `struct Guard<'a>` and `fn install` are module-private; the only construction site is `with_budget`, the guard is bound to `_guard` and never returned, and `PhantomData<Rc<()>>` keeps it `!Send`. Callers can no longer forget a guard, drop one out of order, `mem::forget` one, or move one across threads. This is what upgrades the fix from 'this instance' to 'this class'.
design_conditions_assessment.crate_visible_synchronous_with_budget_Fn: Met, in the same commit: `pub(crate) fn with_budget<T>(b: &QueryBudget, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> T`. `FnOnce` is the right bound — `explain_analyze_with_budget` moves its `String` out of the closure and `construct_or_describe_with_budget` moves the owned `Query` into it. All fourteen production sites and the nine prior test install scopes use it; `install` has no other caller.
design_conditions_assessment.raii_restoration_of_prior_limits_plus_ex: Met and exact. `install` uses `Cell::replace` on both ACTIVE and EXCEEDED and stores both in the guard; `Drop` restores both unconditionally, so return, `?`-error and unwind are covered. Restoration includes `byte_width`, `extra_bytes`, `deadline`, `max_rows`, `max_bytes`, `on` and the parent `cancel` pointer — verified field-by-field by `assert_state`. Top-level behaviour is unchanged (prior state is provably OFF/None outside any frame, since EXCEEDED is only written while `on`). Interaction with `set_width`/`restore_width` around an operator that nests a callback query is correct: the guard restores the parent's width, and the parent's own `restore_width(prev)` still runs afterwards.
design_conditions_assessment.corrected_cancellation_pointer_lifetime_: Met. The old comment's claim ('the Guard lifetime keeps that budget alive until the pointer has been cleared') was the flawed part and is gone. The new argument is frame-based and holds by induction over the private scoped installer: each `cancel` in ACTIVE, and each `previous.cancel` held by a live Guard, is owned by a `QueryBudget` borrowed by a still-live enclosing `with_budget` frame on this thread; snapshots leave the thread only into scoped rayon work that joins inside that frame. Temporary-budget call sites (`with_budget(&QueryBudget::cancelled_by(...), ...)`) are safe because the temporary lives to the end of the enclosing statement. Residual imprecision is NB5 only.
design_conditions_assessment.narrowed_snapshot_visibility: Met. `Limits`, `Limits::why`, `Limits::hit`, `snapshot` and `parallel_json_fanout` moved from `pub(crate)` to `pub(in crate::exec)`; `BYTES_PER_ID`, `set_width`, `restore_width`, `add_bytes`, `exhausted`, `check`, `active`, `cap_alloc`, `remaining_timeout`, `byte_savepoint`, `restore_bytes` and `with_budget` correctly stay `pub(crate)` because they have non-exec callers or no pointer exposure. The snapshot doc now names the four consumers and the invariant a fifth would have to establish. Caveat: I could not verify from the supplied text that no *feature-gated* module outside `crate::exec` references `Limits`/`snapshot` (see CI obligations).
design_conditions_assessment.four_joined_snapshot_consumers_as_truste: Accepted as before, and the code matches the doc: ~2840 scan SELECT-JSON (via `parallel_json_fanout`, `par_chunks().map().collect()` then `budget::exhausted` on the owner thread), ~3039 bindings SELECT-JSON (`collect()` then `budget::check`), ~9102 hash join (`fold`/`reduce` then `budget::exhausted`), ~10070 residual anti-join (`collect::<Result<_,String>>()?` — the `?` cannot escape before the join). The ~2645 parallel materialise path takes no snapshot, so the enumeration of four is correct.
design_conditions_assessment.no_new_arc_tls_or_lifetime_framework: Honoured — the patch adds no allocation, no Arc TLS and no lifetime machinery; the only structural additions are two Guard fields and one wrapper function.

evidence_assessment.sufficiency_for_protected_ci: Sufficient to advance to CI, not to merge. The calibration is honest about its boundaries and I could reconcile every headline number against the code.
evidence_assessment.regression_calibration: The public four-case witness is the discriminating evidence for the issue itself: `baseline_enforced = [true, false, false, true]` is internally consistent with the code — case 1 (no nested call) and case 4 (nested parse error) cannot clobber the outer frame pre-fix because `PreparedQuery::parse` runs before `install`, while cases 2 and 3 (nested ASK, nested ASK with an explicit budget) do reach `install` and therefore disarmed the outer cancellation on the base commit. That matches `public_extension_nested_query_preserves_outer_cancel` exactly.
evidence_assessment.mutation_controls: Useful but narrower than the headline reads. Seven tests ran per control (the seven committed `nested_budget_tests`). `final-omit-limits` fails 5/7, `final-omit-bytes` 3/7, `final-omit-sticky` 1/7 — good, targeted sensitivity for `previous`, `extra_bytes` and `exceeded` respectively. However, `public_extension_nested_query_preserves_outer_cancel` is reported as *passing* under `final-omit-limits`, which is only explicable because that test calls the unmutated linked production library rather than the mutated copied module. So the mutation table does NOT establish the end-to-end regression test's sensitivity; that comes solely from the separate baseline table above. Both together are adequate; either alone would be misleading.
evidence_assessment.test_execution_boundary: The 15/15 module result and the mutation runs were obtained in a task-private copy, not by `cargo test -p sparq-engine` on the committed tree. The committed `#[cfg(test)] mod nested_budget_tests` has, on this evidence, never been compiled or executed inside the real crate under real feature cfgs. Path resolution in the copy (`crate::FunctionRegistry`, `crate::query_with_functions_and_budget`, `oxrdf::{Literal, Term}`, `sparq_core::Graph`) is plausible but not proven identical in-tree. This is the single largest evidence gap and it is exactly a CI job.
evidence_assessment.compilation_coverage: Default features, a six-feature bundle (result-cache, explain-json, params, service-local, vectorized, cs-planner) and a feature-off build all compiled — but these are *builds*, which do not compile `cfg(test)` code, and two of the three ran before the final nine-line cfg(test) addition. Not exercised: the `service` (HTTP) feature, wasm32, `--no-default-features` test compilation, and any other supported feature combination. Because `install`/`Limits`/`snapshot` were `pub(crate)` before and are now private/`pub(in crate::exec)`, any residual reference from a feature-gated module outside `crate::exec` is a hard compile error that only the matrix will surface; `remaining_timeout`'s `cfg_attr(not(feature = "service"), allow(dead_code))` shows such gated callers do exist somewhere.
evidence_assessment.clippy: Direct `clippy-driver -D warnings` on the library under the affected bundle plus the exact final copied budget tests is meaningful but is not `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` across features, as the report itself states.
evidence_assessment.parallel_witness: Establishes only that two distinct Rayon workers really execute one of the four production fanouts under an installed cancellation owner (flag false), using a probe absent from committed source. Correctly not claimed as exhaustive parallel coverage, and no timing/throughput claim is made. It does not, and does not claim to, demonstrate the join-before-return property, which is structural.
evidence_assessment.not_run_anywhere: No workspace tests, no remote SERVICE runtime, no wasm, no Miri/sanitiser, no conformance/coverage/perf ratchets, no `cargo fmt --check`. All are declared. The unsafe pointer path in particular has no checked-model execution anywhere in this evidence set.
evidence_assessment.reviewer_position: I verified none of the hashes, the manifest or any run; I reasoned from the supplied diff and module text alone and report no pass I did not observe.

required_ci_obligations: Full workspace build + `cargo test` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` across the supported feature matrix, explicitly including `--features service` (HTTP) and `--no-default-features`, since the narrowed `pub(in crate::exec)` visibility and the now-private `install` will hard-error on any residual reference from a feature-gated module outside `crate::exec` that was never compiled locally.

First in-tree execution of the committed `exec::budget::nested_budget_tests` via `cargo test -p sparq-engine` under default, all-features and no-default-features, confirming that `crate::FunctionRegistry`, `crate::query_with_functions_and_budget`, `oxrdf::{Literal, Term}` and `Graph::load_str(.., "turtle")` resolve under every supported cfg (the `service`/`service-local` gate on `service_savepoint_brackets_a_fully_returned_nested_budget` and the `not(wasm32)` gate on the deadline test both need to be exercised in both states).

wasm32 target build, plus whatever wasm test job exists: the new tests use `std::thread::scope` and `std::panic::catch_unwind`, which compile but cannot run meaningfully there; confirm they are excluded or gated.

SERVICE gates: remote/HTTP `service` build and runtime, and re-run of the migrated `service_exec_tests` SILENT byte-rollback tests, which are the real consumers of the `byte_savepoint`/`restore_bytes` ordering this patch documents.

Miri (or at minimum a sanitiser run) over the budget module tests — `snapshots_join_two_workers_before_parent_cancel_owner_returns` and `snapshot_is_the_only_signal_a_worker_thread_can_see` are ideal targets — to give the `CancelPtr` raw-pointer/atomic path its first checked-model execution; the unsafe is pre-existing but its justification changed in this commit.

The normal conformance, coverage and performance ratchets, plus the existing timing-sensitive cancellation test `cancel_from_another_thread_stops_large_query_promptly`, to confirm the extra frame save/restore introduces no regression.
Standard review/branch protections; this review is not a merge approval.
limitations: I invoked no tools and ran no build, test, clippy, fmt, Miri or benchmark. Every statement about compilation or test outcomes is either quoted from the supplied report as a claim or is my static reading of the code.

I did not verify the file hashes, the diff hash, the 205-file manifest, or that the supplied text matches commit bcba082; the coordinator's byte-verification is taken as given and is not independently confirmed by me.

I reviewed only the seven changed files' supplied text plus the quoted snapshot/SERVICE excerpts. exec.rs is ~22k lines and I saw a fraction of it; in particular I could not inspect `EngineSnapshot`, `sjoin::BudgetSnapshot`, `set_query_base`, `view_scope`, `trace::install`, `functions`, `local_services`, or any other crate file, so I cannot rule out a reference to `budget::install`/`Limits`/`snapshot` from a module or feature I was not shown. That is the specific residual that the feature-matrix CI obligation is meant to close.

My conclusion that the four snapshot consumers join before their owning frame returns is a structural reading of the rayon combinators used at the four quoted sites; it is not a machine-checked property and does not extend to consumers added later.

I assessed the calibrated evidence for internal consistency and for consistency with the code (notably the `[true,false,false,true]` baseline table and the 7-test mutation counts, which both reconcile); I could not audit the harness that produced it.

Distinguishing introduced from pre-existing: the `CancelPtr` unsafe, the unconditional `Send`/`Sync` impls, the unscoped `set_query_base` TLS, the `restore_bytes` masking of transient sticky reasons, and the un-budget-checked parallel materialise path at ~2645 all predate this commit. This patch introduces no new unsafe code and no new dangling-pointer surface; it narrows the existing one.
